Supportive community

A network of EAs who share advice, resources, and support each other's growth.

Base is a dynamic community of freelance Executive Assistants. All of our EAs are independent contractors, which means you control your hours, your work, and your client relationships. What Base provides is the infrastructure, community, and support to make that work well for everyone.

You are welcome here. Base is dedicated to fostering equity and inclusion across all aspects of identity, background, and experience. We aim to build a community and client base that reflects, supports, and celebrates this diversity.
Commitments

Your commitments as a Base EA

We expect you to honor your agreements with Base and the executives you serve. If you foresee any issues meeting a deadline, please communicate ahead of time and propose a new, realistic timeline.

Please note the following EA commitments, outlined in Schedule 2 of your Base EA contractor agreement:

  • Block fulfillment: You are expected to fill your client's monthly block in full, every month. Executives deserve to receive the full level of support they are paying for, and there are endless ways an EA can proactively create value. It is your responsibility to identify opportunities, anticipate needs, and ensure that your client's hours are fully utilized.
    • If more hours are needed, always communicate directly with the client before going over.
  • Minimum commitment: Commit to at least 4 months with each new client (unless the client or Base ends the partnership sooner).
  • Time tracking: Track all hours worked in the time tracker (in the talent portal).
  • Onboarding plan: Complete the "First 30 Days Onboarding Plan" and deliverables (found in Teachable) when you are matched with a new client.
  • Client paperwork: Some clients require NDAs, data security agreements, or other paperwork. Be prepared to sign what's needed to begin work.
  • Weekly updates: Share hours used with your client weekly to ensure transparency.
  • Transition process: If you are leaving a Base client, inform Base first and follow the transition process outlined in the "Client transitions" section of this course.
  • Stay engaged: Participate in Base community resources (primarily on Slack) to continue your professional learning and to stay connected to your peers.
  • Boost your profile: Client testimonials strengthen your profile and increase your chances of future matches.
    • You are strongly encouraged to include at least one client testimonial on your profile!

Getting matched

How matching works at Base

Open the talent portal
Overview of matching
How matching works at Base

The 5-step matching process

1
Mark your interest

Log into the talent portal and mark your interest in any clients you'd like to work with. There's no limit; our Talent team will only present you to one active client at a time unless you've discussed otherwise.

2
The talent team identifies top matches

Our team reviews your profile, interest statement, time zone, areas of expertise, and client preferences to determine the best fits.

3
The client reviews two EA profiles

The client receives two profiles from our Talent team and decides whether to request a GTKY call. The client may also decline both and request new options at any time.

4
Get-to-know-you (GTKY) calls

If selected by the client, you'll attend a 15-minute GTKY call. These brief conversations gauge chemistry, communication style, and alignment before anyone commits. If it doesn't feel right, that's okay. These calls exist to ensure a mutual fit.

5
The client makes their final selection

After GTKY calls, the client selects their EA, or requests new options until they're ready to move forward.

What happens after?

If you're selected

You'll receive an email notification. Click through to accept the opportunity before moving forward. Once accepted, the Talent team sets up your tools and sends the New client onboarding checklist.

If you're not chosen

You'll still receive an email. You'll remain in the talent cloud and are encouraged to keep marking interest in other clients. Every EA in the cloud is exceptional. Please don't be discouraged.

Kick-off timeline

1
Accept your offer

Click through the offer email and accept. The Talent team will set up your tools and send the New client onboarding checklist.

2
Receive your introduction

Base will introduce you to your executive via email. From this point, scheduling the kick-off call is your responsibility.

3
Schedule the kick-off call

Reply to the introduction email to confirm day and time, then send a calendar invite to your executive with a video conferencing link included.

4
You're off

We completely trust you to manage your client and your work. The Talent team is always available if you need support.

Questions about matching? Reach out to talent@basehq.com. We're always happy to help.

Headshot guidelines

A professional headshot is a key part of making a strong first impression. Here's what to keep in mind:

Avoid AI-generated headshots. They're often easy to spot and may not look like you. If a client recognizes the photo as AI-generated, or if you show up to a GTKY call looking noticeably different from your headshot, it can negatively impact your chances of being selected. Always use a real, recent photo.
Framing
  • Chest up, looking directly at the camera
  • Even lighting on your face, no shadows
Background
  • Clean, neutral background
  • Plain wall or nature work well
  • Avoid distracting elements
Lighting
  • Well-lit location
  • Indoors: avoid backlighting
  • Outdoors: find "open shade"
Attire
  • Office-appropriate clothing
  • Avoid busy textures or logos
  • Keep accessories minimal
Format
  • High-resolution (300 ppi)
  • JPEG or PNG, max 8MB
  • Ideal: 600-800px
While you wait
  • Keep your profile up to date
  • Mark interest in available clients
  • Visit Base HQ for EA resources
If your capacity or availability changes, email talent@basehq.com and we'll update your profile accordingly.

Your first month

The first 30 days onboarding plan

Open course

The first 30 days are crucial in establishing a strong EA-Executive relationship. This course, available on Teachable, is designed to help you hit the ground running.

Course access

You'll be enrolled automatically when matched with a client who ordered this course. No access yet? Email talent@basehq.com.

Billing for the course

Bill ~3 hours to Base (Base Internal Requests First 30 Days Course) for taking the course, and ~3 hours to your client for deliverable work.

$1 pay increase

After 30 days, your executive rates their experience. A score of 8, 9, or 10 earns you a $1 increase in your pay rate, effective the 1st of the following month.

Getting started

Before the kick-off call, open the agenda document below to guide your conversation and capture the information you'll need for the deliverables.

Client deliverables

When matched with a client who has ordered this course, you'll create and share three deliverables. These are due promptly; your executive is expecting them.

1
Executive blueprint

Due the day after the kick-off call. Created using information gathered during the call with the Kick-Off call agenda document.

2
30-day action plan

Also due the day after the kick-off call. Sets the roadmap for your first month together.

3
Summary of accomplishments

Shared at the end of your first 30 days. To create it, make a copy of your 30-Day Action Plan and rename it Summary of Accomplishments: 30 Days, then annotate to show what was completed.

Track your time

The time tracker is the primary method for reporting hours worked with each client. Hours logged form the basis for invoicing and your monthly pay, so log promptly.

Watch the walkthrough

A few minutes here will save you time later. The walkthrough covers logging time, using timers, and managing your entries inside the talent portal.

Time tracker walkthrough

A closer look at the time tracker built into the talent portal. See how to log time, use timers, and manage your entries.

Watch demo
All hours must be entered by EOD on the last day of the month to ensure accurate invoicing through Wingspan. Anything logged after the deadline won't pay out in that cycle. To log time for a previous month, add it as a new entry in the current month.

Two ways to log time

Use a timer

Start and pause as you work, similar to other tools.

Log manually

Enter time for any date, with multiple or custom tasks in a single entry.

Things to know about timers

  • Timers can only be used for the current calendar day
  • Each timer supports a single selected task
  • Timers do not stop automatically
  • Only one timer can run at a time, starting a new one stops the active one

Logging manually

Manual entries support multiple tasks per entry, including custom tasks. Custom tasks you enter are remembered for future entries, so you only have to type them once.

Building trust with new clients. A single monthly entry technically works, but we strongly recommend a more granular daily cadence, or using timers, when starting with a new client or whenever a client wants extra transparency.

Managing your entries

Update or delete entries at any time. The dashboard shows the past two weeks by default. To view or edit older entries, click See more at the bottom of the dashboard for a dedicated history view with search and date filtering.

What's coming

A browser extension is in development (similar to the previous time-tracking browser extension), and the tracker may eventually integrate directly into Base Delegate. Feature requests are welcome, share them in #tool_support on Slack and tag @bence.

Questions about the time tracker? Email talent@basehq.com or post in #tool_support on Slack.

Getting started with Wingspan

Getting started with Wingspan
Invoicing and payments

Wingspan is Base's invoicing platform for contractor payments, plus access to health insurance and financial services. Once matched with your first client, look for this email:

"Base invited you to onboard via Wingspan". Your invitation link is inside. Don't skip it.
  1. Click Get started in the invitation email.
  2. Create your account and enter all required information.
  3. Add your SSN or Tax ID# (required even with an LLC or Sole Partnership).
Already have a Wingspan account? Your setup will skip the info-gathering step.

How Wingspan works

1st
1st of each month

Your tracked hours are sent to Base and Wingspan. Your invoice becomes available to review.

10th
Deadline: 10th of each month

Log into Wingspan and click Accept Invoice. Missing this deadline may push payment back by one month.

15th
15th of the following month

Payment is issued. Example: July hours are paid on August 15th.

Set a recurring calendar event or Slackbot reminder around the 8th so you never miss the approval deadline.

Disputes and one-time payments

If your invoice is incorrect, select Dispute invoice instead of Accept. Write a detailed message. It goes directly to Base Accounting. Once corrected, return to Wingspan to accept.

Disputes filed close to the 10th deadline may cause a payment delay.

Other payments

Automatic
Success payments

These are added to your invoice automatically. No action needed on your end.

Action required
Reset Specialists

Once complete, email talent@basehq.com with your name, assignment, and payment amount.

Tools you'll use

Base Delegate

Voice-first delegation. Voice in, transcript and tasks out, all in one thread

Download app

Optional, but highly recommended. Using Base Delegate together is one of the strongest signals of partnership success. Fewer dropped requests, less back-and-forth, and a clearer record of what's been asked.

Overview

What it is

Base Delegate is a voice-first delegation app built for the EA, executive partnership. Your executive records a voice memo, and the app instantly turns it into a transcribed thread with extracted action items, so requests don't get lost across texts, Slack, email, and phone calls.

It's the conversation in one place: voice in, transcript and tasks out, the answer stays where you can find it.

What you and your client can do with it

For your executive
  • Send requests by voice, in seconds, even on the go
  • Skip the typing, formatting, and follow-ups
  • See progress on what's been asked without chasing you down
  • Trust that nothing gets dropped
For you (the EA)
  • Get a clean transcript and automatic task list for every request
  • Keep all requests in one organized thread per topic
  • Mark tasks complete so your executive sees real-time progress
  • Reduce ambiguity and follow-up questions
Every conversation. Named, summarized, organized.
Know where things stand at a glance.
Messages, tasks, files. The full picture.
From request to done. All in one thread.
Requests become tasks, without the extra work.
Swipe to see more

Contract renewals and rate negotiations

Contract renewals

Assuming a satisfactory relationship between Base, clients, and an EA, we will invite you to renew your contract with us on an annual basis. You will be prompted with an updated contractor agreement in conjunction with your anniversary of starting with your first Base client.

At Base, we're committed to offering fair, transparent, easily understood, and competitive rates to our EA community of remote professionals.

How to request a rate negotiation

If you're negotiating as part of your annual contract renewal, you can reply directly to your anniversary email with the information outlined below.

If you're negotiating out of cycle, you can email our Talent team (talent@basehq.com) directly with the information outlined below.

Tap to view what to include in your rate negotiation request
  • Your name:
  • Client name(s):
  • Client monthly block(s):
  • Length of relationship, with Base and your client(s):
  • Hourly rate request:
  • Provide evidence of exceptional (above our standard high expectations) performance:
    • Consistent positive client feedback
    • Projects or deliverables your client found to be exceptional
    • Work you do that shows your stellar performance
  • As a summary, tell us about why you feel you deserve a rate increase.
  • Are you comfortable with us contacting your client to confirm their feedback directly? Y/N

If you have any questions about your pay, please contact talent@basehq.com.

How you get paid

Four simple steps, every month. Here's the journey from logged hours to deposit:

1
Get set up
Set up your Wingspan account

2
By end-of-month

All hours must be in the time tracker (in the talent portal) by EOD on the last day of the month. Anything later rolls to next cycle.

3
By the 10th
Approve (or dispute) your invoice

Client travel policy

While Base does not require EAs to travel, we support and encourage it when mutually beneficial. If you're open to traveling, it's important to establish clear expectations before any booking or planning begins. Below are key guidelines for travel-related work.

Before you travel

Set expectations early by gathering key details from your client. Consider asking:

  • Will you be flying or driving?
    • If driving (and unable to work), bill travel time in the time tracker under the client project.
    • If working during transit (e.g. layovers), bill only for time actually worked.
  • Will there be downtime to support other clients?
  • Will you incur additional work-related expenses (e.g. hotel Wi-Fi)?
  • Does your client have a formal travel policy or budget?
    • Ask about per diem, flight/hotel budgets, rental car needs, and daily work expectations.

Clients are responsible for all travel-related expenses. Whenever possible, use the client's credit card for bookings. Review the "Expense reimbursements" section of this course for more information.

Best practices as you prepare to travel for your client:

  • Flights and transportation: Book via the client's card. Consider linking it to a ride-sharing account (Uber, Lyft) for single-use access.
  • Mileage: If you are driving your own car for client travel, you should be reimbursed for mileage. You can see mileage rates here. If you are claiming mileage, you should not also request reimbursement for fuel.
  • Hotel: Confirm the client's budget and use a credit card authorization form if needed.
    • Note that you may still have to present your own credit card at check-in to cover any incidentals or extra charges.
      • While items like parking and Wi-Fi can be billed to the client, incidentals (such as pay-per-view, mini-bar, and room service) are not reimbursable.
  • Meals: Follow the client's per diem or guidance. Be respectful with client-funded purchases.
  • Change fees: Clients cover any changes due to circumstances outside your control (e.g. cancelled flight requiring an extra night at a hotel).
If you support multiple clients, treat travel days like time off. Communicate your availability with all of your clients and arrange EA coverage as needed.

During travel

Be sure to track expenses and keep receipts, including written records of cash purchases. Throughout your trip, log time in the time tracker per your agreement with the client. Generally:

Billable time
  • Meetings, direct client work, event prep, business meals (e.g. supporting at dinners), Base-related tasks
  • Transit time only if you can't work (e.g. driving)
Non-billable time
  • Optional social events (happy hours, informal meals)
  • Personal time
  • Transit time, if you choose not to work

After travel

If you have paid for any travel expenses that need reimbursement, please follow the "Expense reimbursements" section of this course. In addition, be sure to send your total expense details to your client directly.

Expense reimbursement

Client expenses

Sometimes you will have an expense that the client should reimburse (e.g. a subscription to a tool they've asked you to use, shipping charges for a project). Often you will be reimbursed directly through your client and their company.

In certain circumstances, Base will allow client reimbursements. Please request the client's approval in writing before incurring the expense. Once you've received approval, forward the email confirmation to success@basehq.com (we will have the expense applied to the client's next invoice).

Vacation planning guide

Base offers "standby" coverage for your client while you're out-of-office. If your client wants support from another Base EA, it's important to set expectations around how the back-up EA will be used in your absence.

Quick rule

If your vacation is 3 business days or less, you don't need to offer coverage. You're still responsible for working your client's full monthly block, so plan to make up any missed time on other days.

Tracking your time
  • Bill up to 1.5 hours per client to Base Internal Requests > Vacation coverage planning in the time tracker.
  • Do not log this time under your client's project.
  • Your back-up EA can also bill up to 1.5 hours to the same client project for prep time.
Documentation

Provide clear documentation to the back-up EA covering your work so you can enjoy interruption-free time off.

Your countdown

Plan ahead, step by step

Confirm coverage with your client
4–6 weeks out

If your client would like coverage, complete this form to indicate your time off.

Post for coverage on Slack
4 weeks out

Post in #project_opportunities using the template below to let the Base EA community know you need coverage.

Hello! I'm looking for vacation coverage. Please see details below and let me know if you are available!

  • Client name and company:
  • Coverage dates:
  • Hours per week:
  • Time of day needed online:
  • Common tasks/projects:
  • Tools/systems:
  • Important notes about client:
  • If you receive multiple responses, choose whichever EA you'd like.
  • Once you select an EA, email talent@basehq.com.
  • Trouble finding someone? Email talent@basehq.com for help.
  • Let your client know who will be providing coverage.
Prep your handoff materials
3–4 weeks out
  • Identify projects and tools your back-up EA will need access to.
  • Identify which projects you can tackle before your time off begins.
  • Write SOPs and key processes for your back-up EA.

  • Ask them to reach out to the client contact(s) on day one of coverage.
  • Remind your client of your coverage plan and vacation dates.

Short-term leave

If you're welcoming a new family member, managing a health issue, or need extended time away for personal reasons, you're encouraged to take a short-term leave. Base will work with you to develop a plan, arrange temporary client coverage, and support your return when you're ready.

To get started, fill out the short-term leave survey. Questions? Email talent@basehq.com.

Client transitions

It is Base's policy that any EA who wishes to terminate work on a Base client account provides a 2-week notice directly to Base. To do so, send an email to both success@basehq.com and talent@basehq.com outlining the details and reasons behind the request (more information below).

We aim to match clients and EAs for long-term compatibility, but if challenges arise, we prioritize troubleshooting before approving a transition. If a transition is needed, the 2-week notice begins on the next business day, assuming Base's internal team is available to receive the request.

If an EA would like to transition away from their client, the EA must notify Base before informing the client. If a transition is initiated by the client, Base will manage the process directly.

Select a transition type to view the full process:

EA-initiated

Transitions initiated by the EA

Follow each step below to ensure a smooth handoff for both you and your client.

1
Inform Base of your decision

Send an email to talent@basehq.com and provide the following details:

  • Your client's full name and company
  • How long you've been working with the client
  • The reason you'd like to transition away from your client
  • The ideal date you'd like to be done working with the client
2
Decide when to notify the client

We strongly encourage you to be the one to share the transition news with your client. Typically, EAs share their news during a check-in call.

  • Once you've determined the date and time you'll inform the client, send that information to talent@basehq.com and success@basehq.com.
  • If you're uncomfortable personally sharing the news, email both talent@basehq.com and success@basehq.com to let Base know.

Regardless of who notifies the client, it's crucial for Base to stay informed and in the loop. This enables us to coordinate our communications with clients effectively.

3
Notify your client

On the call with your client, be sure to discuss the following:

  • Your last day working with the client
  • Any outstanding projects you intend to complete
  • Next steps with Base:
    • You will schedule a call for your client to discuss next steps with Base (see Step 4)
    • Base will send over a client match form for the client to fill out
    • Base will prioritize their matching process to ensure seamless coverage
4
Schedule a call between your client and Base

Use this booking link to schedule a 30-minute call with your client and Base's Success team to discuss next steps. Let the client know that Base is happy to answer any questions they may have on this call.

5
Create an EA to client transition guide

Review and update the current client information you have on file, including communication preferences, working styles, calendar and travel preferences, SOPs, and general documentation.

  • Make a copy of the EA to Client Transition Guide and fill it out to the best of your ability.
  • This document will be shared with the incoming EA.
6
Complete the transition process

Once your client is informed and the transition process is underway, the matching team will start looking for a new EA for the client.

  • Any information you've shared with Base will be shared with the incoming EA.
  • If you have insights about the client that could be helpful to the matching team, please share them with talent@basehq.com.
  • If you plan to onboard the incoming EA (as noted in your transition guide), they will reach out to you directly to get started.
  • Base will reach out to you for any additional requests, if necessary.

In terms of client offboarding tasks:

  • Base will remove you from your client's project in the time tracker and from the Base software workspace once the transition is complete.
  • Any additional offboarding steps should be discussed directly with your client, since this typically involves closing out existing projects and shutting down tool access.
7
Prepare for a new client match

If you're interested in being matched with a new client, log into the talent portal to update your EA profile (including your updated capacity for client work).

  • You may also want to consider adding professional certificates, sample projects, and testimonials to your profile.

If you have any questions or need additional support throughout this process, please reach out to talent@basehq.com.

We understand that transitions can be tough, and we want you to feel supported throughout. Please reach out to talent@basehq.com with any questions or concerns regarding your transition.
Client-initiated

Transitions initiated by the client

Note: While we do request that clients provide their EAs with a 2-week notice, the decision to transition (and when) will ultimately be up to the client. Often, clients request transitions when there are issues related to performance, so prolonging the client and EA relationship may not be advisable in such cases.

Clients, like EAs, may choose to initiate a transition for various reasons. Once a client notifies Base of their desire for a transition, they can either inform the EA directly or request the Base team to do so on their behalf. Similar to an EA-initiated transition, we encourage our clients to communicate the news directly with you.

In order to provide seamless EA coverage to clients, there are rare instances where Base will have already identified a new EA for the client by the time you receive the news of the transition. More often, however, you'll be informed of the transition before the new matching process begins.

EA to client transition guide

  • If your client has asked you to stay on and help train the incoming EA, make a copy of the EA to Client Transition Guide and fill it out to the best of your ability.
    • This document will be shared with the incoming EA.
    • If you're uncertain how much detail to provide, feel free to reach out to talent@basehq.com for advice.
  • If your client has not asked you to help train the incoming EA, no action is needed here.

Prepare for a new client match

  • If you're interested in being matched with a new client, log into the talent portal to update your EA profile (including your updated capacity for client work).
    • Consider adding professional certificates, sample projects, and testimonials to your profile.
We understand that transitions can be tough, and we want you to feel supported throughout. Please reach out to talent@basehq.com with any questions or concerns regarding your transition.

Signing legal documents

Legal paperwork is typically handled during the Base sales process. Occasionally, a client may ask you directly to sign something. As a Base contractor, you are not obligated to sign anything.

1
Ask for context

Find out why the client needs the document signed and what it covers.

2
Share with Base

Email a copy to success@basehq.com and talent@basehq.com.

3
Proceed only with approval

Base will let you know if it's appropriate for you to sign. You are never required to sign without Base's review and approval.

Gifts from clients

Whether or not you need to take action depends entirely on the type of gift your client sends.

Allowed

Non-monetary gifts

Flowers, snacks, branded swag, holiday cards, a bottle of wine, anything that isn't cash.

No action needed. Enjoy them!
Action required

Monetary gifts

Cash, checks, gift cards, Venmo, anything with a dollar value, must be processed through Base to stay compliant.

100% of the gift still goes to you, Base just handles the paperwork.

Receiving a monetary gift? Reach out to success@basehq.com and we'll take care of it.
